sanskrit: atha ye sahitā vṛkṣāḥ saṃghaśaḥ supratiṣṭhitāḥ te hi śīghratamān vātān sahante 'nyonyasaṃśrayāt
english: But those trees that stand together in a grove, firmly rooted, endure even the swiftest winds by leaning upon one another.

sanskrit: evaṃ manuṣyam apy ekaṃ guṇair api samanvitam śakyaṃ dviṣanto manyante vāyur drumam ivaikajam
english: In the same way, enemies think they can destroy a man standing alone, however many his virtues, just as the wind can fell a solitary tree.

sanskrit: anyonyasamupaṣṭambhād anyonyāpāśrayeṇa ca jñātayaḥ saṃpravardhante sarasīvotpalāny uta
english: By mutual support and by sheltering one another, kinsmen flourish, just as lotuses thrive in a lake.

sanskrit: avadhyā brāhmaṇā gāvaḥ striyo bālāś ca jñātayaḥ yeṣāṃ cānnāni bhuñjīta ye ca syuḥ śaraṇāgatāḥ
english: Brahmins, cows, women, children, and kinsmen must never be slain, nor those whose food one has eaten, nor those who have sought one's refuge.

sanskrit: na manuṣye guṇaḥ kaś cid anyo dhanavatām api anāturatvād bhadraṃ te mṛtakalpā hi rogiṇaḥ
english: There is no virtue in a man, however wealthy, that surpasses being free from disease — may it be well with you — for the sick are as good as dead.

sanskrit: avyādhijaṃ kaṭukaṃ śīrṣarogaṃ; pāpānubandhaṃ paruṣaṃ tīkṣṇam ugram satāṃ peyaṃ yan na pibanty asanto; manyuṃ mahārāja piba praśāmya
english: O great king, drink and be calmed — drink wrath, that bitter ailment of the head, born without disease, sharp, harsh, and fierce, attended by sin, the drink that the good imbibe and the wicked refuse.

sanskrit: rogārditā na phalāny ādriyante; na vai labhante viṣayeṣu tattvam duḥkhopetā rogiṇo nityam eva; na budhyante dhanabhogān na saukhyam
english: Those tormented by illness pay no heed to the fruits of action; they cannot experience the truth of pleasures. The sick, always oppressed by pain, are aware of neither the enjoyment of wealth nor of happiness.

sanskrit: purā hy ukto nākaros tvaṃ vaco me; dyūte jitāṃ draupadīṃ prekṣya rājan duryodhanaṃ vārayety akṣavatyāṃ; kitavatvaṃ paṇḍitā varjayanti
english: O king, once before you did not heed my words when, having seen Draupadī won at dice, I told you to restrain Duryodhana in the gambling hall — wise men shun cheating at dice.

sanskrit: na tad balaṃ yan mṛdunā virudhyate; miśro dharmas tarasā sevitavyaḥ pradhvaṃsinī krūrasamāhitā śrīr; mṛduprauḍhā gacchati putrapautrān
english: That is no strength which fights against the gentle; dharma, mixed with vigor, must be practiced. Prosperity assembled through cruelty is soon destroyed, while prosperity built on gentleness combined with firmness passes on to sons and grandsons.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ pāṇḍavān pālayantu; pāṇḍoḥ sutās tava putrāṃś ca pāntu ekārimitrāḥ kuravo hy ekamantrā; jīvantu rājan sukhinaḥ samṛddhāḥ
english: May the sons of Dhritarashtra protect the Pandavas, and may the sons of Pandu protect your sons. Let the Kurus be of one enemy and one counsel; may they live, O king, in happiness and prosperity.

sanskrit: meḍhībhūtaḥ kauravāṇāṃ tvam adya; tvayy ādhīnaṃ kurukulam ājamīḍha pārthān bālān vanavāsaprataptān; gopāyasva svaṃ yaśas tāta rakṣan
english: You are today the central pillar of the Kauravas; the Kuru house depends on you, O descendant of Ajamidha. Protect the young sons of Pritha, scorched by their forest exile — protect them, dear one, guarding your own honor.

sanskrit: saṃdhatsva tvaṃ kauravān pāṇḍuputrair; mā te 'ntaraṃ ripavaḥ prārthayantu satye sthitās te naradeva sarve; duryodhanaṃ sthāpaya tvaṃ narendra
english: Make peace between the Kauravas and the sons of Pandu; let not enemies exploit the breach between you. They are all steadfast in truth, O lord of men — do you yourself restrain Duryodhana, O king of kings.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca saptadaśemān rājendra manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvo 'bravīt vaicitravīrya puruṣān ākāśaṃ muṣṭibhir ghnataḥ
english: Vidura said: O king of kings, Manu, the self-born's son, spoke of these seventeen men, O son of Vichitravīrya, as those who beat the air with their fists.

sanskrit: tān evendrasya hi dhanur anāmyaṃ namato 'bravīt atho marīcinaḥ pādān anāmyān namatas tathā
english: He called them like one who bows while claiming Indra's bow cannot be bent, or like one who bows while saying the feet of Marichi cannot be made to bow.

sanskrit: yaś cāśiṣyaṃ śāsati yaś ca kupyate; yaś cātivelaṃ bhajate dviṣantam striyaś ca yo 'rakṣati bhadram astu te; yaś cāyācyaṃ yācati yaś ca katthate
english: He who instructs one unfit to learn, he who grows angry at the wrong time, he who overly serves an enemy, he who does not protect women — may it be well with you — he who begs from one who should not be begged, and he who boasts.

sanskrit: yaś cābhijātaḥ prakaroty akāryaṃ; yaś cābalo balinā nityavairī aśraddadhānāya ca yo bravīti; yaś cākāmyaṃ kāmayate narendra
english: He who, though well-born, does what should not be done; he who, being weak, is always at war with the strong; he who speaks to one who has no faith; he who desires what is undesirable, O lord of men.

sanskrit: vadhvā hāsaṃ śvaśuro yaś ca manyate; vadhvā vasann uta yo mānakāmaḥ parakṣetre nirvapati yaś ca bījaṃ; striyaṃ ca yaḥ parivadate 'tivelam
english: He who, as father-in-law, takes pleasure in his daughter-in-law's laughter; he who, while living with his daughter-in-law, is desirous of honor; he who sows seed in another's field; and he who slanders a woman excessively.

sanskrit: yaś caiva labdhvā na smarāmīty uvāca; dattvā ca yaḥ katthati yācyamānaḥ yaś cāsataḥ sāntvam upāsatīha; ete 'nuyānty anilaṃ pāśahastāḥ
english: He who, having received something, says 'I do not remember it'; he who boasts when asked for a gift after giving; he who in this world seeks the favor of the wicked — these men are followed by the wind with a noose in hand.

sanskrit: yasmin yathā vartate yo manuṣyas; tasmiṃs tathā vartitavyaṃ sa dharmaḥ māyācāro māyayā vartitavyaḥ; sādhv ācāraḥ sādhunā pratyudeyaḥ
english: Whatever way a man behaves toward another, in the same way should one behave toward him — that is dharma. One who acts with deceit should be met with deceit; one who acts virtuously should be met with virtue.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca śatāyur uktaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvavedeṣu vai yadā nāpnoty atha ca tat sarvam āyuḥ keneha hetunā
english: Dhritarashtra said: A man is said in all the Vedas to live a hundred years — when he does not attain all that lifespan, what is the cause of it here on earth?

sanskrit: vidura uvāca ativādo 'timānaś ca tathātyāgo narādhipa krodhaś cātivivitsā ca mitradrohaś ca tāni ṣaṭ
english: Vidura said: Excessive speech, excessive pride, and likewise excessive abandonment, O lord of men, excessive anger, excessive curiosity, and betrayal of friends — these are the six.

sanskrit: eta evāsayas tīkṣṇāḥ kṛntanty āyūṃṣi dehinām etāni mānavān ghnanti na mṛtyur bhadram astu te
english: These sharp weapons cut short the lifespans of embodied beings — these things kill men, not death itself — may it be well with you.

sanskrit: viśvastasyaiti yo dārān yaś cāpi gurutalpagaḥ vṛṣalīpatir dvijo yaś ca pānapaś caiva bhārata
english: He who violates the wife of one who trusts him, he who sleeps with his guru's wife, the brahmin who has married a low-caste woman, and he who is addicted to drink, O Bharata —

sanskrit: śaraṇāgatahā caiva sarve brahmahaṇaiḥ samāḥ etaiḥ sametya kartavyaṃ prāyaścittam iti śrutiḥ
english: — and he who kills one who has sought refuge — all these are equal to slayers of brahmins. The Vedic teaching declares that expiation must be performed by those who associate with such persons.

sanskrit: gṛhī vadānyo 'napaviddhavākyaḥ; śeṣānnabhoktāpy avihiṃsakaś ca nānarthakṛt tyaktakaliḥ kṛtajñaḥ; satyo mṛduḥ svargam upaiti vidvān
english: The householder who is generous, whose speech is never contemptible, who eats only the remnants of food, who is harmless, who does nothing purposeless, who has abandoned strife, who is grateful, truthful, and gentle — such a wise man attains heaven.

sanskrit: sulabhāḥ puruṣā rājan satataṃ priyavādinaḥ apriyasya tu pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ
english: O king, men who always speak pleasantly are easy to find; but one who speaks what is unpleasant yet wholesome, and one who listens to it, are both rare.

sanskrit: yo hi dharmaṃ vyapāśritya hitvā bhartuḥ priyāpriye apriyāṇy āha pathyāni tena rājā sahāyavān
english: He who, relying on dharma and setting aside the lord's likes and dislikes, speaks what is unpleasant yet wholesome — with such a man the king has a true ally.

sanskrit: tyajet kulārthe puruṣaṃ grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet grāmaṃ janapadasyārthe ātmārthe pṛthivīṃ tyajet
english: For the family's sake abandon a man; for the village's sake abandon a family; for the kingdom's sake abandon a village; for the sake of one's own self abandon the whole earth.

sanskrit: āpadarthaṃ dhanaṃ rakṣed dārān rakṣed dhanair api ātmānaṃ satataṃ rakṣed dārair api dhanair api
english: Protect wealth against calamity; protect one's wife even at the cost of wealth; protect oneself always, even at the cost of wife and wealth.

sanskrit: uktaṃ mayā dyūtakāle 'pi rājan; naivaṃ yuktaṃ vacanaṃ prātipīya tadauṣadhaṃ pathyam ivāturasya; na rocate tava vaicitravīrya
english: I spoke thus also at the time of the dicing, O king, and yet you did not accept such fitting counsel — like a sick man, O son of Vichitravīrya, it did not please you, though it was wholesome medicine.

sanskrit: kākair imāṃś citrabarhān mayūrān; parājaiṣṭhāḥ pāṇḍavān dhārtarāṣṭraiḥ hitvā siṃhān kroṣṭukān gūhamānaḥ; prāpte kāle śocitā tvaṃ narendra
english: You let crows defeat these splendid peacocks — these Pandavas were defeated by the sons of Dhritarashtra — while hiding jackals and abandoning lions. When the time comes, you shall grieve, O lord of men.

sanskrit: yas tāta na krudhyati sarvakālaṃ; bhṛtyasya bhaktasya hite ratasya tasmin bhṛtyā bhartari viśvasanti; na cainam āpatsu parityajanti
english: He, dear one, who does not anger at any time toward a servant who is devoted and intent on his master's welfare — in such a master do servants place their trust, and they do not abandon him in times of calamity.

sanskrit: na bhṛtyānāṃ vṛttisaṃrodhanena; bāhyaṃ janaṃ saṃjighṛkṣed apūrvam tyajanti hy enam ucitāvaruddhāḥ; snigdhā hy amātyāḥ parihīnabhogāḥ
english: One should not try to win outsiders by cutting off the livelihood of one's servants — for ministers who are loving but deprived of their customary enjoyments will abandon such a master, accustomed as they are to their due.

sanskrit: kṛtyāni pūrvaṃ parisaṃkhyāya sarvāṇy; āyavyayāv anurūpāṃ ca vṛttim saṃgṛhṇīyād anurūpān sahāyān; sahāyasādhyāni hi duṣkarāṇi
english: Having first carefully enumerated all undertakings, and income and expenditure, and a livelihood proportionate to them, one should then gather helpers suited to the work — for difficult tasks are accomplished with the aid of helpers.

sanskrit: abhiprāyaṃ yo viditvā tu bhartuḥ; sarvāṇi kāryāṇi karoty atandrīḥ vaktā hitānām anurakta āryaḥ; śaktijña ātmeva hi so 'nukampyaḥ
english: He who, knowing his master's intent, carries out all tasks without laziness — a devoted, noble speaker of what is beneficial, one who knows his own capacity — such a man, like one's very self, deserves compassion.

sanskrit: vākyaṃ tu yo nādriyate 'nuśiṣṭaḥ; pratyāha yaś cāpi niyujyamānaḥ prajñābhimānī pratikūlavādī; tyājyaḥ sa tādṛk tvarayaiva bhṛtyaḥ
english: But a servant who, when instructed, disregards the command, who talks back when assigned a task, who is conceited about his own wisdom and speaks contrarily — such a servant should be dismissed without delay.

sanskrit: astabdham aklībam adīrghasūtraṃ; sānukrośaṃ ślakṣṇam ahāryam anyaiḥ arogajātīyam udāravākyaṃ; dūtaṃ vadanty aṣṭaguṇopapannam
english: They say a messenger endowed with eight qualities is: unhaughty, not timid, not dilatory, compassionate, smooth in manner, not to be bought by others, healthy in constitution, and noble in speech.

sanskrit: na viśvāsāj jātu parasya gehaṃ; gacchen naraś cetayāno vikāle na catvare niśi tiṣṭhen nigūḍho; na rājanyāṃ yoṣitaṃ prārthayīta
english: A wise man should never go to another's house out of blind trust, especially at an improper time; he should not linger concealed in a public square at night; nor should he court a woman of the warrior class.

sanskrit: na nihnavaṃ satragatasya gacchet; saṃsṛṣṭamantrasya kusaṃgatasya na ca brūyān nāśvasāmi tvayīti; sakāraṇaṃ vyapadeśaṃ tu kuryāt
english: He should not become an accomplice in concealing what happened in a sacrifice; nor of one who has shared secret counsel with bad associates. He should not say 'I have no trust in you'; rather, let him give a reason for his refusal.

sanskrit: ghṛṇī rājā puṃścalī rājabhṛtyaḥ; putro bhrātā vidhavā bālaputrā senājīvī coddhṛtabhakta eva; vyavahāre vai varjanīyāḥ syur ete
english: A king who is squeamish, a servant of the king who is unchaste, a son, a brother, a widow with young children, a soldier, and one who has had his rations taken away — these should all be avoided in business dealings.

sanskrit: guṇā daśa snānaśīlaṃ bhajante; balaṃ rūpaṃ svaravarṇapraśuddhiḥ sparśaś ca gandhaś ca viśuddhatā ca; śrīḥ saukumāryaṃ pravarāś ca nāryaḥ
english: Ten qualities attend one who is devoted to bathing: strength, beauty, clarity of voice and complexion, touch, fragrance, purity, auspiciousness, delicacy, and the best of women.

sanskrit: guṇāś ca ṣaṇmitabhuktaṃ bhajante; ārogyam āyuś ca sukhaṃ balaṃ ca anāvilaṃ cāsya bhaved apatyaṃ; na cainam ādyūna iti kṣipanti
english: Six qualities attend one who eats in moderation: health, long life, happiness, strength, clean progeny, and men do not reproach him saying 'he is gluttonous.'

sanskrit: akarmaśīlaṃ ca mahāśanaṃ ca; lokadviṣṭaṃ bahumāyaṃ nṛśaṃsam adeśakālajñam aniṣṭaveṣam; etān gṛhe na prativāsayīta
english: One should not lodge these persons in one's house: one who is idle, a glutton, one hated by the world, one full of deceit, one who is cruel, one who does not know the right place and time, and one who is ill-dressed.

sanskrit: kadaryam ākrośakam aśrutaṃ ca; varākasaṃbhūtam amānyamāninam niṣṭhūriṇaṃ kṛtavairaṃ kṛtaghnam; etān bhṛśārto 'pi na jātu yācet
english: Even in severe distress, one should never beg from these: a miser, one who reviles others, one without learning, one born of a wretched family, one who claims respect while deserving none, one who is harsh, one who bears grudges, and the ungrateful.

sanskrit: saṃkliṣṭakarmāṇam atipravādaṃ; nityānṛtaṃ cādṛḍhabhaktikaṃ ca vikṛṣṭarāgaṃ bahumāninaṃ cāpy; etān na seveta narādhamān ṣaṭ
english: One should not associate with these six lowest of men: one whose deeds are corrupt, one who speaks too much, one who is habitually false, one whose devotion is unstable, one whose attachment is prolonged in wrong directions, and one who is excessively proud.

sanskrit: sahāyabandhanā hy arthāḥ sahāyāś cārthabandhanāḥ anyonyabandhanāv etau vinānyonyaṃ na sidhyataḥ
english: Undertakings are bound by helpers, and helpers are bound by undertakings — these two are bound to each other, and neither succeeds without the other.

sanskrit: utpādya putrān anṛṇāṃś ca kṛtvā; vṛttiṃ ca tebhyo 'nuvidhāya kāṃ cit sthāne kumārīḥ pratipādya sarvā; araṇyasaṃstho munivad bubhūṣet
english: Having fathered sons and freed himself from debt, having arranged some livelihood for them, and having properly given all daughters in marriage, a man should desire to dwell in the forest like a sage.

sanskrit: hitaṃ yat sarvabhūtānām ātmanaś ca sukhāvaham tat kuryād īśvaro hy etan mūlaṃ dharmārthasiddhaye
english: What is beneficial to all beings and conducive to one's own happiness — a capable man should do that, for this is the root of the attainment of dharma and wealth.

sanskrit: buddhiḥ prabhāvas tejaś ca sattvam utthānam eva ca vyavasāyaś ca yasya syāt tasyāvṛttibhayaṃ kutaḥ
english: He who possesses intelligence, power, energy, courage, enterprise, and determination — from what source could there be any fear of poverty for him?

sanskrit: paśya doṣān pāṇḍavair vigrahe tvaṃ; yatra vyatherann api devāḥ saśakrāḥ putrair vairaṃ nityam udvignavāso; yaśaḥpraṇāśo dviṣatāṃ ca harṣaḥ
english: See the faults in going to war with the Pandavas — a conflict wherein even the gods together with Indra would be shaken. Eternal enmity with your sons, a life of constant anxiety, destruction of glory, and joy for your enemies.

sanskrit: bhīṣmasya kopas tava cendrakalpa; droṇasya rājñaś ca yudhiṣṭhirasya utsādayel lokam imaṃ pravṛddhaḥ; śveto grahas tiryag ivāpatan khe
english: The wrath of Bhishma, your own wrath equal to Indra's, the wrath of Drona, and the wrath of King Yudhishthira, fully roused, would destroy this world, like a white planet falling aslant across the sky.

sanskrit: tava putraśataṃ caiva karṇaḥ pañca ca pāṇḍavāḥ pṛthivīm anuśāseyur akhilāṃ sāgarāmbarām
english: Your hundred sons, Karna, and the five Pandavas together could rule the entire earth girdled by the ocean.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrā vanaṃ rājan vyāghrāḥ pāṇḍusutā matāḥ mā vanaṃ chindhi savyāghraṃ mā vyāghrān nīnaśo vanāt
english: The sons of Dhritarashtra are the forest, O king, and the sons of Pandu are considered the tigers — do not cut down the forest along with its tigers, and do not destroy the tigers apart from the forest.

sanskrit: na syād vanam ṛte vyāghrān vyāghrā na syur ṛte vanam vanaṃ hi rakṣyate vyāghrair vyāghrān rakṣati kānanam
english: There would be no forest without tigers, and there would be no tigers without the forest — the forest is protected by the tigers, and the tigers are protected by the forest.

sanskrit: na tathecchanty akalyāṇāḥ pareṣāṃ vedituṃ guṇān yathaiṣāṃ jñātum icchanti nairguṇyaṃ pāpacetasaḥ
english: The wicked do not wish to discern the virtues of others as much as those evil-minded ones wish to discover the absence of virtue in them.

sanskrit: arthasiddhiṃ parām icchan dharmam evāditaś caret na hi dharmād apaity arthaḥ svargalokād ivāmṛtam
english: One who desires the highest attainment of wealth should first and foremost practice dharma — for wealth does not depart from dharma any more than nectar departs from the world of heaven.

sanskrit: yasyātmā virataḥ pāpāt kalyāṇe ca niveśitaḥ tena sarvam idaṃ buddhaṃ prakṛtir vikṛtiś ca yā
english: He whose self has ceased from sin and is established in what is good — by him all this is understood, both nature and its modifications.

sanskrit: yo dharmam arthaṃ kāmaṃ ca yathākālaṃ niṣevate dharmārthakāmasaṃyogaṃ so 'mutreha ca vindati
english: He who properly pursues dharma, wealth, and desire each in its proper time — the combination of dharma, wealth, and desire — attains that both here and hereafter.

sanskrit: saṃniyacchati yo vegam utthitaṃ krodhaharṣayoḥ sa śriyo bhājanaṃ rājan yaś cāpatsu na muhyati
english: He who restrains the impulse that arises from anger and joy, and he who is not bewildered in times of calamity — such a man is a vessel of prosperity, O king.

sanskrit: balaṃ pañcavidhaṃ nityaṃ puruṣāṇāṃ nibodha me yat tu bāhubalaṃ nāma kaniṣṭhaṃ balam ucyate
english: Learn from me of the five kinds of strength that are always present in men. What is called physical strength — strength of the arm — is said to be the lowest strength.

sanskrit: amātyalābho bhadraṃ te dvitīyaṃ balam ucyate dhanalābhas tṛtīyaṃ tu balam āhur jigīṣavaḥ
english: The acquisition of good ministers — may it be well with you — is said to be the second strength. The acquisition of wealth, those who desire conquest say, is the third strength.

sanskrit: yat tv asya sahajaṃ rājan pitṛpaitāmahaḥ balam abhijātabalaṃ nāma tac caturthaṃ balaṃ smṛtam
english: What is the innate strength of a man, O king, descended from father and grandfather — that is called the strength of noble birth and is remembered as the fourth strength.

sanskrit: yena tv etāni sarvāṇi saṃgṛhītāni bhārata yad balānāṃ balaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tat prajñābalam ucyate
english: But that by which all these are gathered together, O Bharata — that which is the best of all strengths — is called the strength of wisdom.

sanskrit: mahate yo 'pakārāya narasya prabhaven naraḥ tena vairaṃ samāsajya dūrastho 'smīti nāśvaset
english: When a man is capable of doing great harm to another man, having incurred his enmity, one should not take comfort saying 'I am far away.'

sanskrit: strīṣu rājasu sarpeṣu svādhyāye śatruseviṣu bhoge cāyuṣi viśvāsaṃ kaḥ prājñaḥ kartum arhati
english: What wise man should place trust in women, in kings, in serpents, in Vedic recitation, in those who serve enemies, and in pleasure and in life?

sanskrit: prajñāśareṇābhihatasya jantoś; cikitsakāḥ santi na cauṣadhāni na homamantrā na ca maṅgalāni; nātharvaṇā nāpy agadāḥ susiddhāḥ
english: For a creature struck by the arrow of wisdom, there are no healers, no medicines, no oblation-mantras, no auspicious rites, no Atharvavedic remedies, not even highly perfected antidotes.

sanskrit: sarpaś cāgniś ca siṃhaś ca kulaputraś ca bhārata nāvajñeyā manuṣyeṇa sarve te hy atitejasaḥ
english: A serpent, fire, a lion, and a son of good family, O Bharata — none of these should be treated with contempt by a man, for all of them are of exceeding power.

sanskrit: agnis tejo mahal loke gūḍhas tiṣṭhati dāruṣu na copayuṅkte tad dāru yāvan no dīpyate paraiḥ
english: Fire, that great power in the world, lies hidden in wood and does not consume that wood as long as it is not kindled by others.

sanskrit: sa eva khalu dārubhyo yadā nirmathya dīpyate tadā tac ca vanaṃ cānyan nirdahaty āśu tejasā
english: But when that same fire is churned forth from wood and blazes up, it then swiftly burns both that wood and all the forest around it with its energy.

sanskrit: evam eva kule jātāḥ pāvakopamatejasaḥ kṣamāvanto nirākārāḥ kāṣṭhe 'gnir iva śerate
english: In just the same way, those born in noble families, whose energy is like fire, patient and showing no outward sign, lie dormant like fire in wood.

sanskrit: latādharmā tvaṃ saputraḥ śālāḥ pāṇḍusutā matāḥ na latā vardhate jātu mahādrumam anāśritā
english: You and your sons have the nature of creepers, while the sons of Pandu are considered the great sala trees — no creeper ever grows without leaning on a great tree.

sanskrit: vanaṃ rājaṃs tvaṃ saputro 'mbikeya; siṃhān vane pāṇḍavāṃs tāta viddhi siṃhair vihīnaṃ hi vanaṃ vinaśyet; siṃhā vinaśyeyur ṛte vanena
english: You and your sons are the forest, O king, O son of Ambika, and know the Pandavas to be the lions in the forest, dear one — for a forest without lions would perish, and the lions would perish without the forest.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca ūrdhvaṃ prāṇā hy utkrāmanti yūnaḥ sthavira āyati pratyutthānābhivādābhyāṃ punas tān pratipadyate
english: Vidura said: The vital breaths of a young man actually rise upward when an elder approaches, and through standing to receive him and through respectful salutation, he recovers them again.

sanskrit: pīṭhaṃ dattvā sādhave 'bhyāgatāya; ānīyāpaḥ parinirṇijya pādau sukhaṃ pṛṣṭvā prativedyātmasaṃsthaṃ; tato dadyād annam avekṣya dhīraḥ
english: Having offered a seat to the virtuous guest who has arrived, having brought water and washed his feet, having inquired after his welfare and informed him of one's own condition — then let the wise man give food after duly attending to him.

sanskrit: yasyodakaṃ madhuparkaṃ ca gāṃ ca; namantravit pratigṛhṇāti gehe lobhād bhayād arthakārpaṇyato vā; tasyānarthaṃ jīvitam āhur āryāḥ
english: He in whose house water, the honey-mixture, and the cow are received by a guest without the proper mantras — whether out of greed, fear, or parsimony for the sake of wealth — the noble declare his life to be a life of futility.

sanskrit: cikitsakaḥ śalyakartāvakīrṇī; stenaḥ krūro madyapo bhrūṇahā ca senājīvī śrutivikrāyakaś ca; bhṛśaṃ priyo 'py atithir nodakārhaḥ
english: A physician, a surgeon, one who has broken his vow of chastity, a thief, a cruel man, a drunkard, one who kills an embryo, one who lives by military service, and one who sells his Vedic learning — however dear such a guest may be, he does not deserve the water-offering.

sanskrit: avikreyaṃ lavaṇaṃ pakvam annaṃ; dadhi kṣīraṃ madhu tailaṃ ghṛtaṃ ca tilā māṃsaṃ mūlaphalāni śākaṃ; raktaṃ vāsaḥ sarvagandhā guḍaś ca
english: Things that should not be sold are: salt, cooked food, curds, milk, honey, oil, clarified butter, sesame seeds, meat, roots and fruits, vegetables, red garments, all fragrant substances, and molasses.

sanskrit: aroṣaṇo yaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcanaḥ; prahīṇaśoko gatasaṃdhivigrahaḥ nindāpraśaṃsoparataḥ priyāpriye; carann udāsīnavad eṣa bhikṣukaḥ
english: He who is free from anger, who looks on clod and gold as equal, who has relinquished grief, who has gone beyond both alliance and conflict, who has ceased from blame and praise alike, who is indifferent to the pleasant and the unpleasant — such a wandering mendicant walks as one who is neutral.

sanskrit: nīvāramūleṅgudaśākavṛttiḥ; susaṃyatātmāgnikāryeṣv acodyaḥ vane vasann atithiṣv apramatto; dhuraṃdharaḥ puṇyakṛd eṣa tāpasaḥ
english: He who subsists on wild rice, roots, ingudi nuts, and vegetables, who is well self-controlled, who needs no prompting in the rites of the sacred fire, who lives in the forest and is ever attentive to guests, who bears the burden of austerity, and who performs meritorious acts — he is the true ascetic.

sanskrit: apakṛtvā buddhimato dūrastho 'smīti nāśvaset dīrghau buddhimato bāhū yābhyāṃ hiṃsati hiṃsitaḥ
english: Having wronged a man of wisdom, one should not take comfort saying 'I am far away' — the arms of a wise man are long, and with them he strikes the one who has struck him.
